DISCOVER · READ · GROW

AKSHARA
Complete Code Companion

A file-by-file, workflow-by-workflow explanation of the implementation completed through commit de9d4fc

Scope: 99 changed files · approximately 7,259 additions · backend, frontend, security, persistence and tests
Prepared for: Ayush Thakur and the Akshara project team
Generated: 3 August 2026

How to Use This Companion

This is not a marketing report. It is a teaching document intended to let you explain the implementation in a viva, debug it without guessing, and safely extend it later. Read Chapters 1–15 first. They explain why the system is shaped this way and trace complete requests. Then use the annotated appendix when opening a particular source file in the editor.

Exact scope. The appendix covers every file added or modified between commits 48cdd34 and de9d4fc. That is the implementation phase that connected hybrid import, catalogue operations, fulfilment, My Books, private uploads, review management and discussions. Existing authentication/cart foundations are explained where they participate in these flows.

Three questions to ask about every line

  1. Which layer owns this decision? UI, controller, service, repository, entity or configuration?
  2. What state can it change? Browser state, HTTP state, database state, inventory, order history or a private file?
  3. What protects it? Validation, JWT role, ownership query, transaction, uniqueness constraint, lock, test or error handler?

Reading Java syntax

SyntaxMeaning
@AnnotationMetadata interpreted by Spring, Jakarta Validation, JPA or JUnit.
recordImmutable request/response carrier with generated accessors.
finalThe reference cannot be reassigned after construction.
Optional<T>A value may be present or absent; callers must handle both.
stream().filter().map()A pipeline that selects and transforms collection elements.
throwStops normal flow and delegates error translation upward.

Reading React syntax

SyntaxMeaning
useStateStores a value between renders and supplies a setter.
useEffectRuns synchronization work such as an API request after rendering.
useMemoRecomputes derived data only when dependencies change.
{condition && <UI />}Renders UI only when the condition is truthy.
awaitPauses the async function until a promise settles.
setState(previous => ...)Safely calculates the next state from the previous state.

1. System Architecture

Browser / React / Vite
        │  JSON, multipart upload, JWT Bearer token
        ▼
Spring MVC Controllers
        │  validated DTOs
        ▼
Application Services ───────────────► Open Library
        │                              metadata only
        ▼
Spring Data Repositories
        │
        ├────────► MySQL: catalogue, users, commerce, community
        └────────► Private filesystem: reader-owned PDF/EPUB files

The browser is deliberately not trusted with business decisions. React decides what to display and which request to send. Spring Security decides whether the caller may enter an endpoint. Controllers translate HTTP into Java inputs. Services enforce rules. Repositories load and persist state. Entities model relational data. DTOs prevent internal entity graphs from leaking into JSON.

Why the frontend does not call Open Library

If React called Open Library directly, provider JSON would leak into the UI, duplicate detection would be impossible before import, provider errors would vary, and a malicious caller could bypass Akshara’s normalization. The backend provider isolates all of this. The public catalogue never depends on Open Library availability because imported books are read from MySQL.

Dependency direction

Controllers depend on services; services depend on repositories and provider interfaces; repositories depend on JPA. The provider interface is important because a later Google Books adapter can be added without changing controller contracts. React pages depend on service modules rather than duplicating Axios calls.

2. Security and Identity

Akshara uses stateless JWT authentication. Login produces a token whose subject is the user ID and whose role claim is converted to ROLE_READER or ROLE_ADMIN. Every protected request sends Authorization: Bearer …. The shared Axios interceptor attaches it automatically.

Endpoint familyAuthorityReason
/api/public/**, /api/auth/**AnyoneDiscovery and authentication must be reachable before login.
/api/admin/**AdminPrice, stock, import, deletion and fulfilment affect the entire store.
Cart, wishlist, checkout, orders, library, review writesReaderThese resources belong to a signed-in reader.

Frontend route guards improve navigation but are not security boundaries. A user can manually send HTTP requests, so Spring Security and ownership-aware repository queries must enforce the rule again. Personal books use findByIdAndUser_Id; orders are queried with both order ID and user ID; review/reply mutation checks the author.

Why IDs come from the token

A request must not say “perform this operation for user 7” and expect trust. Services parse the authenticated JWT subject, load that enabled user and derive ownership internally. This prevents horizontal privilege escalation.

3. Hybrid Catalogue Import

Search sequence

Admin types title/author/ISBN
→ BookImportPage.handleSearch
→ adminBookService.searchExternalBooks
→ GET /api/admin/book-import/search
→ AdminBookImportController.search
→ ExternalBookSearchService.search
→ OpenLibraryBookMetadataProvider.search
→ GET https://openlibrary.org/search.json
→ normalize each work/edition
→ query MySQL for ISBN duplicates
→ return normalized results to React

The provider requests only selected fields to reduce response size. Offset is calculated as (page - 1) × size. A custom User-Agent includes the configured contact because external services need identifiable responsible clients. Connect/read timeouts prevent a slow provider from holding a server thread indefinitely.

Normalization

Open Library may place ISBN, publisher, page count or publication date on either a work or an edition. Mapping prefers edition data and falls back to work data. ISBN characters are cleaned; the first 10- and 13-character candidates are selected. Subjects are bounded so a single noisy provider record cannot create hundreds of local categories. Cover IDs become Cover API URLs.

Permanent import

Selected external metadata
        +
Admin-owned format, SKU, price, stock, availability
        ↓
POST /api/admin/book-import
        ↓
@Transactional BookImportService
        ├─ find/create Authors
        ├─ find/create Categories
        ├─ find/create Publisher
        ├─ validate ISBN and SKU uniqueness
        ├─ create Book
        ├─ create BookEdition
        └─ create Inventory
        ↓
Public catalogue reads the stored book from MySQL

The external API never decides price or stock. The transaction is essential: a book without its edition/inventory is unusable, so partial persistence must roll back. Manual entry calls the same save path but does not require an external identity and may relax ISBN requirements for rare books.

Seed operation

The seed endpoint is explicit and Admin-only. It searches eight broad genres, balances results across them, skips entries without ISBNs, derives predictable demonstration prices/stock/SKUs, and marks an initial subset featured. It does not run automatically at startup; therefore normal boots never scrape or unexpectedly mutate the catalogue.

4. Catalogue and Inventory Administration

A Book represents the conceptual title. A BookEdition represents a specific format/publication/ISBN. Inventory belongs to an edition because different editions can have different price, stock and availability. This separation is the reason an “Atomic Habits” paperback and hardcover can be managed independently.

Exact update versus restock

  • Inventory update replaces price, total quantity, availability and active status with the submitted values.
  • Restock adds units to the existing quantity while holding a database lock. It never accidentally replaces 10 units with 5 when the intention was “add five.”

Availability normalization prevents contradictory state. Zero stock cannot remain IN_STOCK; adding stock to OUT_OF_STOCK restores IN_STOCK; deliberately UNAVAILABLE inventory stays unavailable until an admin changes it.

Safe deletion

Catalogue deletion must consider carts, wishlists, reviews and historical orders. Temporary references may be removed. Historical order items instead preserve immutable snapshots such as title, ISBN, format and price. Their optional live edition link is detached so deleting a catalogue entry cannot erase or corrupt an old receipt.

5. Cart, Checkout and Orders

The cart stores an edition and quantity, not merely a book ID. Adding checks that the edition is active, sellable and sufficiently stocked. Checkout locks/validates inventory, creates an address snapshot, order, order items and payment, reduces stock and clears the cart in one transaction.

Why order snapshots exist

Catalogue values can change after purchase. An order must continue showing what the customer actually bought at the original price. OrderItem therefore stores title, cover, format, ISBN, publisher and unit-price snapshots rather than rendering an old order from mutable catalogue data.

Fulfilment state machine

PLACED → CONFIRMED → PROCESSING → SHIPPED → DELIVERED
   └────────────── cancellation allowed before shipping ──────┘

The backend owns allowed transitions. React only presents valid next actions. Cancellation restores reserved stock. Delivering a cash-on-delivery order marks payment paid. Skipping directly from PLACED to SHIPPED or reversing a delivered order produces a 400 response.

6. My Books and Private Uploads

My Books combines two different ownership concepts without confusing them. Purchased physical editions come from non-cancelled order items and show fulfilment status. Personal uploads are reader-owned files stored privately and served only after an ownership check.

Upload safety

  • Maximum size is enforced by Spring multipart configuration and the service.
  • The extension alone is not trusted: PDF must begin with %PDF-; EPUB must be a ZIP whose first entry is the correct mimetype.
  • The original filename is sanitized for display only.
  • The stored filename is a generated UUID.
  • The resolved path must remain inside the configured storage root.
  • Database rows are queried by both file ID and owner ID.
  • Failed persistence cleans up the copied file.

A physical purchase deliberately does not unlock a copyrighted digital file. PDF uploads open using an authenticated Blob response. EPUB currently downloads because a complete EPUB reader is outside this implementation.

7. Reviews, My Reviews and Discussions

A review is a rated reflection attached to one user and one book. My Reviews makes ownership visible by providing edit/delete controls. Community displays recent reviews and can expand a reply thread under each one.

Replies are separate entities because a review remains the stable root of conversation. Each reply records its review, author, content and creation time. Creating and deleting replies requires a Reader JWT; deletion verifies that the current user wrote the reply. Public users can read conversations without acquiring mutation rights.

Frontend behavior

Community loads a bounded recent feed, derives counts/average locally, and supports client-side search/sort. DiscussionThread loads replies on demand, posts a new reply, updates local state and allows the author to delete their own reply. Empty/loading/error states prevent the earlier “section that does nothing” experience.

8. React Application Structure

App.jsx is the route table. Navbar and Footer remain outside the route switch. RouteErrorBoundary wraps routed content. ProtectedRoute requires authentication; AdminRoute requires the Admin role.

RouteResponsibility
/, /books/:idPublic discovery and book evaluation.
/wishlist, /cart, /checkoutReader commerce preparation.
/orders, /orders/:idReader receipts and physical delivery journey.
/my-books, /my-reviewsPersonal library and owned contributions.
/communityPublic reader reviews and conversations.
/admin/books/importExternal metadata import and manual entry.
/admin/booksCatalogue/inventory operations.
/admin/ordersOrder confirmation and fulfilment.

State placement

Local page state holds form fields, loading/error flags and selected records. AuthProvider owns the session. ReaderDataProvider owns cart/wishlist data that is shared across navigation. Service modules own HTTP syntax, which keeps pages focused on user interaction.

9. API Client Design

The Axios instance uses relative /api

Admin and reader service modules are intentionally small: each function describes one backend operation. Normalization in adminBookService tolerates different external-result shapes at one boundary rather than scattering nullish checks across the import page.

10. Error Handling and Validation

Validation occurs at several levels because each level knows different facts:

  1. HTML attributes give immediate usability feedback.
  2. React prevents empty actions and displays backend messages.
  3. DTO annotations validate structure and limits.
  4. Services validate database-dependent rules such as duplicate ISBN or legal state transitions.
  5. Database constraints provide the final concurrency-safe boundary.

GlobalExceptionHandler produces stable statuses: 400 malformed/invalid input, 401 invalid authentication, 403 denied access, 404 missing resource, 409 duplicate/conflict, 413 upload too large, 500 storage/internal failure and 503 external catalogue unavailability.

11. Persistence Model

AppUser ── Cart ── CartItem ── BookEdition ── Inventory
   │                                  │
   ├── WishlistItem ── Book           ├── Publisher
   ├── Review ── ReviewReply          └── Book ── Authors / Categories
   ├── PersonalBook
   └── Order ── OrderItem snapshots ── optional live BookEdition

Relationships express ownership. Join entities model many-to-many book-author and book-category links explicitly. Inventory is one-to-one with an edition. Order snapshots deliberately duplicate selected values because historical truth is more important than normalization for receipts.

12. Automated Tests

The verified backend suite contains 74 passing tests. Controller tests use MockMvc to prove HTTP status, JSON shape, validation and role rules. Service unit tests mock repositories/providers to isolate business branches. BookImportServiceIntegrationTest uses Spring/JPA with H2 to prove transactional persistence and uniqueness behavior. Provider tests use a local mock HTTP server rather than relying on Open Library during the test run.

The essential testing pattern is Arrange–Act–Assert: create controlled state; call one behavior; inspect result and side effects. Mockito verify proves that invalid requests do not reach dangerous collaborators. Integration tests complement mocks by checking real mappings and constraints.

13. Configuration and Operational Boundaries

Secrets come from environment variables. Database passwords and JWT secrets are intentionally absent from source control. Open Library configuration exposes contact identity and timeouts. Private file storage has a configurable root and multipart limits. The ignored storage directory prevents personal files entering Git.

ddl-auto=update, local filesystem storage, cash-on-delivery simulation and the lack of a Google Books adapter are deliberate current limitations, not hidden completed features.

14. How to Explain the Project in a Viva

  1. Start with the problem: discovery, commerce, ownership and conversation are fragmented.
  2. Explain the roles and one complete Reader/Admin journey.
  3. Draw the layered architecture and say why business rules live in services.
  4. Demonstrate metadata versus inventory using Open Library and Akshara-owned fields.
  5. Show one transaction: import or checkout.
  6. Show one ownership rule: personal file, order or reply.
  7. Show order snapshots and state transitions.
  8. Show tests and state the honest limitations.
Core distinction: Open Library describes books. Akshara decides what it sells, at what price, in which format, with how much stock, and how that purchase continues into the reader’s private shelf and community participation.

15. Current Gaps and Safe Extension Points

  • Add Flyway migrations before treating the schema as production-managed.
  • Add React component and end-to-end workflow tests.
  • Add reading status, progress, notes and goals to complete “Discover · Read · Grow.”
  • Add a Google Books provider through BookMetadataProvider rather than modifying controllers.
  • Add community pagination, notifications and moderation.
  • Move private files to managed object storage for deployment.
  • Add real payment webhooks only behind a provider interface and idempotent transaction handling.

These are extension points, not reasons to rewrite working modules. Preserve endpoint contracts and move new rules into focused services.

 132  title, ISBN, format and price snapshots; their optional live-edition link is
 133  detached before catalogue deletion so order history remains readable.

 917      private boolean hasValidIsbn10Checksum(String isbn) {
 918          int sum = 0;
 919          for (int index = 0; index < 10; index++) {
 920              char character = isbn.charAt(index);
 921              int value = character == 'X' ? 10 : character - '0';

 923          }
 924          return sum % 11 == 0;

 927      private boolean hasValidIsbn13Checksum(String isbn) {
 928          int sum = 0;
 929          for (int index = 0; index < 12; index++) {
 930              int value = isbn.charAt(index) - '0';
 931              sum += value * (index % 2 == 0 ? 1 : 3);
 932          }

 934          return checkDigit == isbn.charAt(12) - '0';
 935      }

 142      private List<String> strings(JsonNode node, String field) {

 149      private String uniqueSlug(String name) {
 150          String base = Normalizer.normalize(name, Normalizer.Form.NFD)
 151                  .replaceAll("\\p{M}", "")
 152                  .toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)
 153                  .replaceAll("[^a-z0-9]+", "-")
 154                  .replaceAll("(^-|-$)", "");
 155          if (base.isBlank()) base = "category";
 156          if (base.length() > 110) base = base.substring(0, 110).replaceAll("-$", "");
 157          String candidate = base;
 158          int suffix = 2;
 159          while (categoryRepository.existsBySlugIgnoreCase(candidate)) {
 160              candidate = base + "-" + suffix++;
 161          }
 162          return candidate;

 121      private BookFormat detectAndValidateFormat(String filename, MultipartFile file) {
 122          String lower = filename.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
 123          try (InputStream input = file.getInputStream()) {
 124              byte[] signature = input.readNBytes(5);
 125              if (lower.endsWith(".pdf") && signature.length >= 5
 126                      && signature[0] == '%' && signature[1] == 'P' && signature[2] == 'D'
 127                      && signature[3] == 'F' && signature[4] == '-') {
 128                  return BookFormat.PDF;
 129              }
 130              if (lower.endsWith(".epub") && signature.length >= 2
 131                      && signature[0] == 'P' && signature[1] == 'K'
 132                      && hasEpubMimeType(file)) {
 133                  return BookFormat.EPUB;
 134              }

 141      private boolean hasEpubMimeType(MultipartFile file) throws IOException {
 142          try (ZipInputStream zip = new ZipInputStream(file.getInputStream())) {
 143              var firstEntry = zip.getNextEntry();
 144              if (firstEntry == null || !"mimetype".equals(firstEntry.getName())) return false;
 145              String mimeType = new String(zip.readNBytes(30), StandardCharsets.US_ASCII).trim();
 146              return "application/epub+zip".equals(mimeType);
 147          }
 148      }

 150      private String safeOriginalFilename(String filename) {
 151          if (filename == null || filename.isBlank()) return "personal-book";
 152          String normalized = filename.replace('\\', '/');
 153          String safe = normalized.substring(normalized.lastIndexOf('/') + 1)
 154                  .replaceAll("[\\p{Cntrl}]", "_");
 155          if (safe.isBlank()) safe = "personal-book";
 156          return safe.length() > 255 ? safe.substring(safe.length() - 255) : safe;
 157      }

  91  
  92      private String isbn13(int value) {
  93          String firstTwelve = "978" + String.format("%09d", value);
  94          int sum = 0;
  95          for (int index = 0; index < firstTwelve.length(); index++) {
  96              int digit = firstTwelve.charAt(index) - '0';
  97              sum += digit * (index % 2 == 0 ? 1 : 3);
  98          }
  99          return firstTwelve + ((10 - sum % 10) % 10);
 100      }
 101  }
 102

  53  export async function searchExternalBooks(query, source = 'OPEN_LIBRARY') {
  54    const response = await api.get('/admin/book-import/search', {
  55      params: { query: query.trim(), source },
  56      timeout: 30000,
  57    })
  58    return unwrapResults(response.data).flatMap((item) => {
  59      const editions = item.editions ?? item.variants
  60      return Array.isArray(editions) && editions.length
  61        ? editions.map((edition) => normalizeEdition(edition, item))
  62        : [normalizeEdition(item)]
  63    })
  64  }
  65
